seo.description: Loft conversions in Basildon, Laindon and Pitsea. The rear dormer gives the most room for your money on a standard house. Planning and building regs handled. Free site visit

image.alt: Loft conversion on a family home in Basildon by J Berry Construction

paragraphs: If you want the most room from a loft for the least outlay, the rear dormer is usually how you get it, and on Basildon's many post-war and inter-war semis and terraces it is the workhorse conversion. A box dormer built out across the back of the roof turns a cramped, sloping loft into a full-height double room, often with space for an ensuite, using the roof you already have. We convert lofts across Basildon, Laindon, Pitsea and the surrounding area, and on a standard family house this is well-trodden, straightforward work, not the grand, complicated thing people sometimes imagine. Call 07920 731533 or request a callback.

homes.title: Other options for your Basildon roof
homes.intro: The rear dormer is not the only route. Where a Basildon semi has a hipped roof, a hip-to-gable (often combined with a rear dormer) squares it off for even more space; where a loft already has good head height, a simpler rooflight conversion may be enough; and some of the town's later or system-built houses need a closer structural look before committing, which we always do. But for the standard pitched-roof family homes that make up much of Basildon, the rear dormer is the practical, space-maximising default, and we match the approach to your actual roof.

planning.title: Planning in Basildon
paragraphs: Because they sit on the rear roof slope, many rear dormers in Basildon are permitted development, within the volume limits (broadly 40 cubic metres for terraces, 50 for semis and detached) and the conditions, so no planning application is needed. Front dormers, mansards, anything over the limits, and conversions in any local conservation area (such as the older village cores) usually need permission. Every conversion always needs full building-regulations approval, for the structure, the new floor, the staircase and the fire escape, and on a terrace or semi the Party Wall Act usually applies. We check your property's position and handle the planning, party wall and building regulations for you, so the paperwork is not your problem.

whyUs.title: Why homeowners choose us
whyUs.text: Most of Basildon's housing is exactly the kind the rear dormer was made for, so it is worth explaining why it is so often the sensible choice. A rear dormer is a box-shaped structure built out from the back slope of the roof, with a flat or shallow roof of its own. Because it goes straight up and out rather than following the slope, it creates the maximum usable head height and floor area the roof can give, you end up with proper full-height space across most of the room, rather than the pinched, sloping ceilings a rooflight-only conversion leaves. On a typical Basildon semi or terrace, that is the difference between a usable double bedroom and an awkward box room. It is also the most cost-effective way to get that space. A rear dormer avoids the heavier structural work of squaring off a whole hipped roof or the full roof rebuild of a mansard, so on a standard house it gives you the best room for the money, and because it sits on the rear of the roof, it is often permitted development, needing no planning application at all. For a family house where the aim is a good extra bedroom without overspending, it is usually the answer, and it is work we do all the time.

faqs.q: What is a rear dormer, and does it really give the most space?
faqs.a: A rear dormer is a box-shaped structure built out from the back slope of the roof, with its own flat or shallow roof. Because it rises straight up rather than following the roof's slope, it creates the most usable head height and floor area a loft can give, proper full-height space across most of the room, rather than the sloping ceilings of a rooflight-only conversion. On a standard Basildon semi or terrace it is usually the way to get a genuinely usable double room.

faqs.q: Is a loft conversion affordable on a standard Basildon house?
faqs.a: It is one of the more cost-effective ways to add a proper room, especially with a rear dormer, which gives maximum space without the heavier structural work of a hip-to-gable or the full roof rebuild of a mansard. It is also generally cheaper than moving to a larger house once you count moving costs. The exact figure depends on your roof and finish, which is why we give you an itemised quote after a free site visit rather than a headline number.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a rear dormer in Basildon?
faqs.a: Often not. Because a rear dormer sits on the back roof slope, it is frequently permitted development within the volume limits and conditions, so no application is needed. Front dormers, mansards, anything over the limits, and conversions in a conservation area do need permission. Every conversion still needs full building-regulations approval. We check your position and confirm which applies before you commit.

faqs.q: What type of loft conversion suits my Basildon house?
faqs.a: For most of the town's standard pitched-roof semis and terraces, a rear dormer gives the best space for the money; a hipped roof may suit a hip-to-gable, often with a dormer behind; a loft with good head height may need only a rooflight conversion; and some later or system-built houses need a closer structural look first. We match the conversion to your actual roof.

faqs.q: Can my Basildon loft be converted?
faqs.a: Most standard houses can. It comes down to head height (roughly 2.2 to 2.4 metres at the ridge before losing some to the new floor and ceiling), the roof structure, and room for a compliant staircase. A rear dormer often helps where head height is tight, by adding it. We give you a straight answer at the site visit, including on the town's later or non-traditional house types.

faqs.q: Do you also do extensions in Basildon?
faqs.a: Yes. If a loft cannot give you enough space, or you need ground-floor room too, we design and build extensions in Basildon, see our Basildon extension page. We will advise honestly on whether a loft, an extension or both best suits what you are after.
